title: Drum solos, the Big Four and old-time solos
summary: Frazier describes solos by Red Happy and Chinee at the Lyric, the 'Big Four' rhythm section and how old solos differ from today's.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Did they ever use drum solos in them days? You know, like Red Happy and them.

Yeah, yeah. Yeah, yeah. Happy took solos. Yeah, he took solos when he wasn't in the show. He took drum solos. He made special breaks. And they used to feature them a whole lot in the Lyric Theater with whistles. Who, Happy? Red Happy, yeah. Plenty of drums. Plenty of drums.
What kind of drum solos would they take then? How many choruses?

You might take a chorus. A chorus. Well, one chorus or probably two, all the pens. That's what you call the overture, you know. Everybody used to put the spotlight on the drum and they just turn him loose. Then sometimes, too, they used to turn the drum as Chani Babay by himself.
Yeah. I mean, sometimes turn drum solos on advertisements.
Bands meet one there, you see. And then they either turn the drum loose or turn, you used to call the Big Four the rhythm session. That'd be the bass, the banjo, and the drum.

And whether it was a piano, if they used a piano like on a hall, well, the pianists call it the Big Four. They call it sticking the dogs on you. The bass balling, the drum, and the banjo. Sicking the dogs on you, the rhythm section, yeah.
Well, what kind of drum solos would they do? The same as now?
Yeah, well, it might be similar today because these drummers of the day, they make mostly paradiddles, you see.

But them guys made their drum solos with plenty of snare drum rolls and beats and then back to their four car bells and them rattles and all that. But the drummers of the day, they're making a whole lot of paradiddles beats, you know. I mean.
But, I mean, their drum solos would be sort of like those you did with Hammer's band.
Yeah. Mercy's band on Riverside. Yeah. That's one of the old-time drum solos, yeah.
